### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **193** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/oauth2-grant/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**88** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f29a88a87c2140e845bee1c47a40d0846249bb4`.

⛔ **18** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/oauth2-grant/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (4 routes)`, `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 38 pages)`, `/automation/:name (route, 48 pages)`
- **37** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **59** of **211** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f29a88a87c2140e845bee1c47a40d0846249bb4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `235d472fa461f0d13195470ac8e950d40bf66541` — the merge of head `c449914018039db8593440244d8850e8a53fb535` into base `0f29a88a87c2140e845bee1c47a40d0846249bb4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 235d472fa461f0d13195470ac8e950d40bf66541 && git checkout 235d472fa461f0d13195470ac8e950d40bf66541
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0f29a88a87c2140e845bee1c47a40d0846249bb4 c449914018039db8593440244d8850e8a53fb535 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0f29a88a87c2140e845bee1c47a40d0846249bb4 && git merge --no-ff c449914018039db8593440244d8850e8a53fb535

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f29a88a87c2140e845bee1c47a40d0846249bb4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0f29a88a87c2140e845bee1c47a40d0846249bb4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `23bbe3f4e942e764c4c695704e23631695ddb1de`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts, packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/sys-connector-connection.object.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-connections.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/oauth2-grant/authorization.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/oauth2-grant/token-endpoint.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/oauth2-grant/grant-handle.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json, packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json, .changeset/26702-connector-oauth2-connections.md; read on `main` (not reviewed): docs/adr/0143-outbound-connector-auth-is-open-tier.md, packages/spec/src/shared/connector-auth.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/security/capabilities.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/cluster-service.ts, packages/types/src/connector-credential-source.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-scim-connection-credential.object.ts

Review time: 2026-10-31T04:55Z · Card #26702 (p1 · `security` · `domain:server`) · PR #28317 at the head above · ADR-0143 S1 (D3 connection record, D4 per-dispatch resolution, D5 redirect route, D6 pin).

Inputs read: card #26702 body and all 14 comments (triage 6444265744 … os-dev-report 6539138863, the claim 6524120668 as amended 2026-10-31, the slice plan 6524271601); the PR body and file list; the net diff `origin/main...pr-28317` (32 files, +3620/−105); the 50 check-runs on the head.

**Check-runs on the head (the gate verdicts):** 50 runs — 41 `success`, 9 `skipped` (matrix placeholders and opt-in harnesses), 0 failed, 0 in progress at the time of this record. Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Type Check · workspace / source / consumer gates, Test Core 1–8, Build Core, Build Docs: all green.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged:

1. **`@objectstack/spec` public surface, additive.** `IAutomationService` gains four **optional** members (`getConnectorConnection`, `beginConnectorConnection`, `completeConnectorConnection`, `revokeConnectorConnection`) and five exported interfaces (`ConnectorConnectionState`, `ConnectorConnectionRequest`, `ConnectorConnectionBegin`, `ConnectorConnectionCallbackQuery`, `ConnectorConnectionCallbackRequest`). Optional members break no existing implementer (the engine in `engine.ts` and the runtime door both probe `typeof svc.member === 'function'` and answer 501 when absent). `api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json` carry exactly those five names — regenerated, not hand-edited. **Right.**
2. **`PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['service-automation']` += `sys_connector_connection`**, alphabetical order kept, docblock amended. The object is registered in both `plugin.ts` registration lists (full and credential-only), so the conformance pin that ties the constant to a registered object holds. **Right.**
3. **New system object `sys_connector_connection`** (engine-owned, `access: { default: 'private' }`, `apiEnabled: false`, `apiMethods: []`, `trackHistory: false`): columns `organization_id`, `connector_name`, `grant` (closed `authorization_code`), `refresh_token` as `Field.secret()`, `status` (closed `connected | reconnect_required`), `status_reason`, `scopes`, `expires_at`, `revision`, `connected_at`, `connected_by`; unique `connector_name` scoped by `organization`. No access-token column, no registered-client column (deviation 4). Matches ADR-0143 D3 and Q2 = B as scoped. The "declared permission" Q2 borrows from `sys_scim_connection_credential` (`requiredPermissions: ['manage_platform_settings']` there) is carried here by the route gate instead, which is the only path to the row since the data door is closed — the same posture `sys_connector_credential` already takes. **Right.**
4. **Tenancy census** 91 registered / 46 in reach, `sys_connector_connection` in reach by `organization_id`; **ownership inventory** row with fate `attribution` (every row is written with the organization that connected it; a NULL row has no producer). Both follow from the explicit, required, readonly `organization_id` column. **Right.**
5. **Route ledger** +4 rows, `server-only`, census 113; the callback is a literal path mounted ahead of `/:name/connection` in `dispatcher-plugin.ts`, and `isConnectorConnectionDoor` excludes `credential-refs` so the #27237 door keeps its namespace. Not SDK surface (the Console drives it, S4). **Right.**
6. **`registerConnectorProvider(key, factory, { credentialHandle?: boolean })`** — an optional third argument, additive; `providerAppliesCredentialHandle(key)` is a new read. `ConnectorHold` gains `{ kind: 'connection' }` (internal union; `describeHold` extended). New plugin option `connectorOAuthRedirectUri`. All additive. **Right.**
7. **`Metadata-protocol: added`** — a new system object joins the metadata protocol. **Right.** **`Clause-②: yes`** — a published spec change. **Right.**
8. **No change to `packages/spec/src/security/capabilities.ts`, `connector-auth.zod.ts`, or `connector-provider.ts`.** The server consumes S0's shapes (`ConnectorOAuth2GrantSchema`, `ConnectorProviderContext.credentialHandle`, `ConnectorCredentialHandle`) without redefining any — no second Zod source, no handle redefinition. **Right.**

**Claim check (6524120668, amended).** The claim's `packages/spec` surface is three Seam lines: the connection object's name in `platform-object-names.ts` (touched: one entry), a `manage_connector_connections` capability in `capabilities.ts` (not touched), and optional `IAutomationService` members with their result types in `automation-service.ts` (touched: four members, five request/result interfaces). The spec diff **stays within the claim**: two of three named lines are used exactly as named, and the third is left unused (a narrowing, not an excursion). The generated artifacts under `packages/spec/api-surface` and `export-origins` are Human Minimum 6, not Seam lines.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/26702-connector-oauth2-connections.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/service-automation: minor`, `@objectstack/runtime: minor`. What the diff publishes: spec adds optional members and new exports (minor, no removal, no signature change); service-automation adds a system object, a store, a handle, a plugin option and an optional registration argument (minor); runtime adds four routes (minor). **Matches.** The changeset carries `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: added`, both matching the PR body and the claim. ADR-0143 is cited. The changeset text names the new routes, the capability, the no-leak rule and the redirect-URI resolution (`connectorOAuthRedirectUri`, else `OS_AUTH_URL` / `OS_BASE_URL`) — each verified against `plugin.ts#connectorOAuthRedirectUri`. One wording nit: the changeset says "`OS_BASE_URL` (or `OS_AUTH_URL`)" while the code reads `OS_AUTH_URL` first, then `OS_BASE_URL`; the docs page and the ledger row give the code's order. Not a semver matter.

Clause-②: yes.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report (6539138863): `open_questions: []` — nothing to answer. `out_of_scope_findings`: `check:error-code-casing` is a lane gate `dispatch-gates` does not derive for a test file under `packages/runtime/src/domains` — **escalated to tooling** as a gap in the derived-gate family (the dev caught it in CI and fixed it on this head; the PM tooling owner should add the path to the derivation).

The two seat-accepted scope choices and the eight declared deviations in the PR body (plus the three extra ones in the os-dev report that the body folds into its sections) are judged in ④ below; summary dispositions:

| # | deviation | disposition |
|:--|:--|:--|
| (a) | server-only provider opt-in guard, no spec flag; built-ins not opted in until S2 | **accepted** |
| (b) | `app-credential` stays degraded until S2 | **accepted** |
| 1 | `manage_metadata` reused; no `manage_connector_connections` | **accepted (narrowing) + should-fix follow-up** |
| 2 | binding is user + organization, not session | **accepted** |
| 3 | `iss` accepted, not validated | **accepted** (S2 owes validation) |
| 4 | no dynamically-registered-client row | **accepted** (S2) |
| 5 | cross-replica re-judging on the seeing replica only | **accepted** |
| 6 | datasource lending still 422s grant-bearing kinds | **accepted** |
| 7 | callback answers JSON | **accepted** (S4 flag below) |
| 8 | re-materialization only on any-connection ↔ none | **accepted** |
| report-only | pending authorization in cluster KV / memory, unsealed | **accepted + should-fix** |

Flags of my own, for the next slices (not findings against this head):
- **S4:** the callback route is gated by `manage_metadata` on the request's `executionContext`, so the browser landing on `GET …/oauth/callback` must carry the administrator's session (a cookie session works; a bearer-only client would be refused 401 before the state is consumed, and the pending connect waits out its 600 s). The Console flow must land the redirect in a cookie-authenticated browser.
- **S2:** `iss` validation (RFC 9207) once issuer metadata exists; the `registered_client` column (D3) with DCR; dropping the opt-in guard for the built-ins.
- **Tooling:** the `error-code-casing` derivation gap above.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`** — judged against ADR-0143 D3 / D5 (the ruling it implements) and its first consumer (`packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts#respondToConnectorConnectionDoor` → `engine.ts` → `plugin.ts`).

- The four members are optional "for the reason `getConnectorDescriptors` is" — the bare engine answers 503 and the runtime door answers 501 when they are absent; a host that predates them is unaffected. Holds.
- `ConnectorConnectionState` carries no token by construction: `plugin.ts#describeConnection` builds it from `ConnectorConnectionRecord`, whose reader (`connector-connections.ts#toRecord`) reads the masked `refresh_token` only as a boolean `hasRefreshToken`, and that boolean is not even on the state. The runtime door returns the state verbatim. Holds; pinned by the no-leak test (`connector-connection-door.test.ts`, "no token, code, verifier or client secret in a log line, a descriptor, a reason, a door answer or an engine read").
- `ConnectorConnectionCallbackQuery` is exactly the ledger's closed set (`code`, `state`, `error`, `error_description`, `error_uri`, `iss`); the door refuses an unknown key (a `redirect_uri` above all) and a repeated key before the service sees it. Holds.
- Documented rejections vs. the tree: 404 undeclared instance, 400 not-`authorization_code`, 400 no organization, 400 unknown/expired/replayed/foreign `state`, 400 `error` answer naming the registered code only, 503 token endpoint unreachable, 503 no fixed redirect origin, 404 revoke of nothing — each found in `plugin.ts#connectionDoorSubject` / `#completeConnectorConnection` / `#revokeConnectorConnection`. **One mismatch (should-fix S1):** `getConnectorConnection` documents "a deployment that cannot read the store (`503`)", but `ConnectorConnectionStore.read()` returns `undefined` when no data engine is resolvable, so the door answers `status: 'not_connected'` instead of 503 in that case (a thrown engine error does surface as 503 via `connectorCredentialRefusal`). Make `read()` on the door path throw `ConnectorCredentialUnavailableError` when no engine is available, or amend the docblock; declared ≠ enforced otherwise.
- `completeConnectorConnection`'s docblock states the order "state taken once → same user in the same organization → code exchanged with the PKCE verifier → stored"; the implementation follows it exactly (take, expiry, binding, `error` branch, `code` presence, declaration re-read, client secret resolution, exchange, store under the reconcile queue, seed). Holds.

**`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts`** — judged against the object it names and the conformance that reads it. The entry lands with the object in the same PR, in both registration lists, alphabetical, docblock amended. Holds.

**Security properties of the cited code (p1 `security` card — the attack pass):**

1. **Redirect / callback `state` binding and replay.** `state` is 32 random bytes base64url (256 bits); the pending record is keyed by `SHA-256(state)` so the raw state is never a listable key; TTL 600 s in the cluster KV (`ttl` is seconds per `KVSetOptions`) and an explicit `expiresAt` check in `completeConnectorConnection` (covers the memory store, whose `take` does no expiry check of its own); single use by `kv.delete(key, { ifVersion })` or `Map.delete` — a replayed or racing callback finds nothing. The `state` is taken **before** the binding check and the `error` branch, so a refused callback also burns the pending (correct: nothing a second try could legitimately reuse). Tests pin replay, never-begun, expiry, and foreign user/organization. **Holds.**
2. **PKCE.** `S256` always, no switch (D2.1). Verifier 32 random bytes base64url (43 chars, within RFC 7636's 43–128), challenge `base64url(sha256(verifier))`, `code_challenge_method=S256` on the authorization request, `code_verifier` + repeated `redirect_uri` on the exchange. **Holds.**
3. **Binding to user + organization (deviation 2).** Verified on `main`: `packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts` has `userId`, `tenantId`, `systemPermissions`, `isSystem` and no session identifier of any kind, so a session binding is not expressible at this seam. The pending record holds `{ connector, organizationId, userId }`; the callback refuses `callerUser !== pending.userId || callerOrganization !== pending.organizationId` before any exchange, and an `isSystem` or anonymous caller (no `userId`) fails the comparison. The threat D5 names (a code injected into another administrator's callback, RFC 6749 §10.12) is refused; the residual (two sessions of one user in one organization) grants nothing the user does not already hold. **Accepted.**
4. **Cross-organization / cross-user use of a connection.** The door derives the organization from `context.tenantId` only (never from the body or path); a platform-wide caller with no active organization is refused 400. Rows are read `where { organization_id, connector_name }` under a system context; the row written on complete is `pending.organizationId`, which the binding check has already equated to the caller's. At dispatch, `grant-handle.ts#select` reads the row for `request.organizationId`; a request with no organization uses the only connection or is refused 422 naming the count (ADR-0143 D4, last bullet, verbatim). The cache is keyed per organization and invalidated when the row's `revision` moves (`held.revision === record.revision`), so a reconnect in org A never serves org A's old token and never touches org B's. **Holds.** Residual by design of the S0 seam: an opted-in provider that omits `organizationId` from `callWithBorrowedCredential` would fall into the one-connection rule for every run; this is the provider's obligation under the seam's docblock, and the test provider does pass `automation.tenantId`. S2 should pin it for the built-ins.
5. **Token and refresh-token storage.** `refresh_token` is `Field.secret()` (ADR-0100 channel): encrypted at rest, masked on every engine read, dereferenced only through `engine.resolveSecretField` inside `resolveRefreshToken`, whose one caller sends it to the token endpoint. A write that the engine cannot protect (`Cannot persist secret field`) is refused 503 with "Nothing was kept". Access tokens live only in the handle's `Map` / closure; no column, no KV, no log. `markReconnectRequired` nulls the stored token. Writes touch only `sys_connector_connection` and `sys_secret`; nothing named `metadata`, `account`, `session` or `user` is read or written (D6 pin). **Holds.**
6. **The pending-authorization record (deviation "unsealed", report item 11).** The KV value holds `connector`, `organizationId`, `userId`, the PKCE **verifier** in plaintext, `redirectUri` and `expiresAt`, for up to 600 s, under a hashed key. The verifier alone is useless to an attacker: completing a connect additionally needs the authorization code (seen only by the administrator's browser and the vendor) and a request authenticated as the same user in the same organization with `manage_metadata`. An attacker with KV read access is therefore no better off than one without it against this door. The step-1 plan's sealed-`state` design would have removed the server-side record at the cost of carrying the (encrypted) verifier through the browser; both designs meet D5. **Accepted; should-fix (non-blocking):** seal the pending value through the host `ICryptoProvider` (or at least authenticate it) so a KV compromise reveals no OAuth material, and say in `authorization.ts` which trust boundary the KV sits inside.
7. **Refresh-once-on-401.** `callWithBorrowedCredential` (types, on `main`) does get → refresh-if-within-skew → attempt → on 401 refresh → one retry → `credentialRejectedRefusal`. The handle's `refresh` drops the cached token and joins or starts the single flight per instance (`client_credentials`) or per organization (`authorization_code`); with a cluster service the refresh runs under `withLock('connector-connection:…:refresh')` with the row re-read inside, and `recordRefresh` writes the rotated token only over the revision it read, caching nothing when the row moved. `invalid_grant` → `reconnect_required` + token nulled + reconcile re-judge + 503 "reconnect required"; `429`/`5xx`/no answer → `CONNECTOR_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`, connection untouched; `invalid_client`/`unauthorized_client`/401 → 503 naming the configuration. A server that issues no refresh token is marked `reconnect_required` when the access token expires, not retried into existence. **Holds.** **Should-fix (non-blocking):** `recordRefresh` and `markReconnectRequired` are read-then-update, not a conditional update; the invariant relies on the in-process single flight and, across replicas, on `ILock`. A conditional update (`where: { id, revision }`) would make "a rotated token is never overwritten by a stale one" hold without the lock as well.
8. **Error texts.** `token-endpoint.ts` names at most a registered RFC 6749 §5.2 code or an HTTP status, never the server's body; `completeConnectorConnection` names a registered §4.1.2.1 code only and never echoes `error_description` / `error_uri`; `connect()` replaces any engine message ("a foreign message may carry the row it was handed"); the 503 on an unreachable token endpoint carries the module's own fixed sentence. Log lines carry instance, organization and user ids only. The no-leak test asserts seven secrets (client secret, code, verifier, both refresh tokens, both access tokens) absent from logs at `debug`, descriptors, the degraded reason, door answers and an engine read, and asserts the logs are non-empty. **Holds.** The `scopes` string is the server's own text persisted and echoed — ADR D3 lists it as persisted state, so this is by ruling; noted, not a finding.
9. **Capability gating (deviation 1).** ADR-0143 D5: "Who may connect, reconnect or revoke is a capability check the server slice declares." The slice declares `manage_metadata`, fail-closed, `isSystem` bypassing, anonymous refused 401 first, no walled refusal. Against the claim's File surface: the `manage_connector_connections` Seam line was proposed by the seat's own plan "for the contract review to rule on", so leaving `capabilities.ts` untouched is within the claim. Against the card: the credential door (#27237) already lets a `manage_metadata` holder bind a secret to the same instances, so binding a grant is the same privilege class, not a widening; and because the organization is always the caller's active one, a holder cannot connect or revoke another organization's connection. Against ADR-0143: Q1 = A makes the connection the organization's act, which the door honours by dropping the walled gate the credential door keeps (that door writes environment-level rows; this one writes organization rows). **Ruling: accepted as a narrowing for S1.** `manage_metadata` is declared `scope: 'platform'` in `capabilities.ts`, while the act is organization-scoped; that mismatch is tolerable because the organization is taken from the session, not the capability, but it is the reason a dedicated org-scoped capability stays the right end state. **Should-fix (follow-up, before S4 ships the Console flow):** file the `manage_connector_connections` capability with its default grants, eval fixture and widget as its own card; the route starts asking either, which is additive.
10. **Redirect URI.** Fixed per deployment (`connectorOAuthRedirectUri` option, else `OS_AUTH_URL` / `OS_BASE_URL` + the callback path), never read from the request; begin is refused 503 without one. The exchange repeats the same `redirectUri` from the pending record. **Holds.**
11. **Provider opt-in guard (scope choice a).** S0's `ConnectorProviderContext.credentialHandle` docblock leaves it to the factory to fail an instance it cannot authenticate; this slice is stricter: an `oauth2` instance on a provider not registered with `{ credentialHandle: true }` is held degraded naming the provider, so the built-in `rest` / `openapi` / `mcp` factories (which close over a static `auth` they would find `undefined`) can never dispatch it unauthenticated. The `watchForCredentialRejection` and `recordCredentialProven` paths are correctly bypassed for handle-served instances (a 401 there refuses the access token, not the client secret). **Accepted.**
12. **Scheme hardening (should-fix, non-blocking, S1 or S2).** S0's `z.string().url()` admits any scheme. `tokenUrl` over plain `http://` off loopback would send the client secret (Basic) and the refresh token in the clear; `authorizationUrl` with a non-http(s) scheme is answered to the caller as `authorizationUrl` and will be navigated to by the Console in S4. `beginConnectorConnection` (or the materializer's servability check) should refuse a non-https `tokenUrl` / `authorizationUrl` outside loopback, with a located reason. Declarative metadata is a publish-gated, administrator-authored surface, so this is defence in depth, not an open hole.
13. **Revoke (should-fix, non-blocking).** `DELETE …/connection` removes the row and drops the cached token but does not attempt RFC 7009 revocation at the vendor, so the deleted refresh token stays valid at the authorization server until it expires or the administrator revokes it there. Either attempt revocation when the vendor publishes a `revocation_endpoint` (S2 has the discovery) or say so in the ledger row and the docs page.
